title: This Restaurant Was Picked as Maine's Most Romantic Dining Spot - NewsBreak
text:
By Kid ,
12 hours ago
Maine’s most romantic table is calling…and it’s right here! #DateNightGoals
Subscribe to WBZN Old Town Maine on Youtube
Valentine’s Day in Maine is a nice time to go out for a meal. Restaurants are cozy and often have special menus for the holiday. It’s a chance to enjoy good food, maybe a drink or dessert, and spend time with someone you care about.
Lovefood is a popular online food platform that provides recipes, cooking guides, food news, restaurant reviews, and meal planning.
They also make lists, which we love, so when it came down to naming the most romantic restaurant in each state, we had to find out which one they picked for the State of Maine.
Natalie’s Restaurant is an award‑winning, fine‑dining restaurant located at Camden Harbour Inn in gorgeous Camden, Maine. It’s known for sophisticated cuisine that blends modern French and European techniques with the best of Maine’s seasonal and locally sourced ingredients.
Read More: Popular Bangor Food Truck Announces Restaurant Opening Date
The menu changes with the seasons, offering everything from à la carte selections to multi‑course tasting menus and specialty lobster dishes that celebrate the flavors of coastal New England.
A bar and lounge serve lighter fare and drinks, and during the season, guests can enjoy dining on the heated wrap‑around porch overlooking Camden Harbor.
The restaurant has received widespread acclaim, including AAA Four Diamond recognition and a spot on OpenTable’s Top 100 Best Restaurants in America.
The dining room is a combination of elegance and sophistication, making it perfect for Valentine’s Day, or any romantic dinner or special occasion.
An extensive wine list curated for pairing with menus. They also feature a private dining room, which is available for events or celebrations.
Reservations are highly recommended, especially on weekends or during peak season.
Natalie’s is located at 83 Bay View St, Camden. Check out their website for seasonal hours, and more information about this fantastic dining experience.

This festive event honors Moxie, the official state soft drink of Maine MBTV YT Maine Fiddlehead Festival The Maine Fiddlehead Festival is a unique celebration of Maine's iconic fiddlehead ferns, typically held in late May in various locations throughout the state. 61 Maine Restaurants That Closed in 2025 Gallery Credit: Sean McKenna A Coffeehouse via Facebook A Coffeehouse A Coffehouse in Waterville, Maine, announced on Facebook that it would be closing for good on March 30.
The coffee place has only been open about a year, but said the "business model is not economically sustainable" to continue. Google Maps Adams Street Pub According to a Facebook post , Adams Street Pub in Biddeford, Maine, closed on October 27, 2025.
They thanked everyone for "40 years of business, wild nights, memories and one hell of a reputation," while noting that Townhouse Pub remains open.
Adams Street Pub opened in 1985. Ancho Honey via Facebook Ancho Honey Ancho Honey in Tenants Harbor, Maine, announced on a post on Facebook on April 4 that it would be closing for good.
After months of reflection, the owner cited rising costs, staffing challenges, and personal priorities like spending more time with his growing daughters as the main reasons behind the decision.
The takeout restaurant opened in 2019. Anneke Jans via Facebook Anneke Jans Anneke Jans in Kittery, Maine, announced on January 13 on Facebook that it would be closing.
The restaurant had been in that particular building for 20 years.
Read more here. Anthony's Italian Kitchen via Facebook Anthony's Italian Kitchen Anthony's Italian Kitchen in Portland, Maine, announced on Facebook that after 33 years, the restaurant would be closing for good on February 7.
The post revealed that Anthony is retiring while thanking all the "faithful" customers and staff over the years. bakemaine via Instagram Bake Maine According to an Instagram post , Bake Maine announced that its last day in Portland would be on August 27.
The bakery and cafe said that it was going to put full-time focus on its Wells location, noting that it was difficult trying to keep both going at the same time.
Bake Maine opened its Portland spot in 2023 and then its Wells place in May 2024. Bar Futo via Facebook Bar Futo According to a Facebook post , Bar Futo in Portland, Maine, announced it would be closing on November 1, 2025.
The Japanese-inspired restaurant thanked its team and customers but noted that "although this chapter has come to an end, we are not finished with this space. More coming this winter!"
Bar Futo opened in 2022. Betty's Ice Cream via Facebook Betty's Ice Cream Betty's Ice Cream announced in a Facebook post on March 18 that it would be closing for good.
The ice cream shop had only recently opened in May 2024.
On its Facebook page , the business indicated that it served "a variety of Mexican-style and flavor products, including delicious helados and paletas." Google Maps Big Stop Restaurant According to a Facebook post , Big Stop Restaurant in Baileyville, Maine, closed on December 24.
An article from WCYY states that the place has been around since the '80s.
The social media post does note that "there is no interruption to all other services at this location, including fuel, EV charging, convenience store operations as well as amenities for Professional Drivers." bon Vivant via Facebook bon Vivant bon Vivant in Lewiston, Maine, announced with sadness on January 3 on Facebook that it would be closing.
It said the "national trends in the restaurant industry combined with the physical and financial climate of downtown Lewiston has proven not ready for a high-end restaurant."
Read more here. Google Maps Cafe Louis Cafe Louis, which opened in 2021, in South Portland, Maine, closed on February 2, according to WGME .
The news station reported that the cafe's owner had said the lease was up and decided not to renew. Google Maps Carolina Sports & Spirits Carolina Sports & Spirits in Bangor, Maine, which has been around for over 20 years, announced that it would be closing on March 29.
According to a Facebook post , Salt North Taproom will be the new venture at the Union Street location. cocktail_mary via Instagram Cocktail Mary Cocktail Mary in Portland, Maine, celebrated its fifth anniversary in November 2024 and revealed on Instagram around that same time that it would be moving to a new and larger space.
Another Instagram post highlighted that January 28 would be its last day open at the Congress Street location and Cocktail Mary 2.0 would return at a new location at some point in the future.
Read more here. Google Maps Cracker Barrel Cracker Barrel in South Portland, Maine, closed January 21 after 15 years in business, according to News Center Maine .
The news station noted that a Cracker Barrel spokesperson cited "explaining that declining traffic and other challenges after the pandemic made it difficult to sustain operations."
Read more here . Google Maps Crybabies According to the Bangor Daily News , Crybabies in Stonington, Maine, would be closing.
On its Facebook page , the restaurant shared that its last day was September 2. WABI reported that this was the second year Crybabies had been open.
In the Bangor Daily News article , the newspaper reported that the owner was closing this Stonington location and starting a new tavern and bar in Bucksport. Daily Soup via Facebook Daily Soup According to a Facebook post , Daily Soup in Belfast, Maine, announced it would be closing on October 23, the 13th anniversary of the business that started out in the owner's home.
The takeout restaurant shared that with a declining customer base and lackluster tourist season, there were not enough "gains to soldier through another winter."
Daily Soup started in 2012 with the physical restaurant location opening in 2014. definitivebrewing via Instagram Definitive Brewing According to an Instagram post , Definitive Brewing announced its Kittery, Maine, location would close after being open for five years.
Its final day was September 1, 2025.
Thankfully, you can still get your Definitive Brewing fix at its Portland location.
Some of the comments on the brewery's Instagram post sharing the announcement expressed sadness for the closure, but Definitive Brewing expressed that they were "grateful for every beer shared, every story told, and every friendship made here." Dok Mali Noodle Bar via Facebook Dok Mali Noodle Bar According to a Facebook post , Dok Mali Noodle Bar in South Portland announced that its last day would be August 30.
The restaurant, which served a variety of noodle-based soups and dishes, had opened in July 2024.
The Portland Press Herald reported that another pan-Asian restaurant, Asian House, would be taking over the location. Ds Pizza, Pasta & Subs via Facebook Ds Pizza, Pasta & Subs Ds Pizza, Pasta & Subs in Fryeburg, Maine, announced on January 4 on Facebook that it would be closing for good.
It stated that "a combination of factors beyond our control has made it increasingly difficult to continue operating."
Read more here. Google Maps Elevation Burger According to the Portland Press Herald , Elevation Burger opened its first Maine location in 2012 in South Portland.
The organic burger chain quietly closed all of its Maine locations in early April: Augusta, Portland, and South Portland.
According to the restaurant's website , only nine locations are left in the United States, with none in New England. Evenrood's via Facebook Evenrood's According to a Facebook post , Evenrood's in Bangor, Maine, announced it would be closing on December 31.
The restaurant first opened in 2015.
A reason wasn't given for the closure in the post, but the restaurant's owner did note, "We are deeply grateful to our loyal guests, friends, and community for making this journey so special. Your support, stories, and shared meals have meant the world to us." The Frog and Turtle ... a gastro pub via Facebook The Frog and Turtle The Frog and Turtle in Westbrook announced on Facebook in February that it was closing on March 2, in part, due to "financial hardships."
According to WMTW , The Frog and Turtle was Maine's first gastropub and opened in 2007. The Garage BBQ via Facebook The Garage BBQ The Garage BBQ in Scarborough, Maine, announced on its website that it would be closing after eight years.
In the note it said, "It’s been a great run but now it’s time to focus on family – and our other establishments." Goldfinch Creamery Cafe and bakery via Facebook Goldfinch Creamery Cafe and Bakery Goldfinch Creamery Cafe and Bakery in Gardiner, Maine, announced on Facebook it would be closing for good on February 21.
The post revealed the owners were "heartbroken and devastated" but that there was no other choice. The Hamburger Stand via Facebook The Hamburger Stand The Hamburger Stand in Biddeford, Maine, announced its closure on April 16 on Facebook.
Rising costs, increased rent, and post-COVID challenges were cited as the reasons behind the hard decision.
The Route 1 staple opened in 2016. Henry VIII Carvery via Facebook Henry VIII Carvery Henry VIII Carvery in Kittery, Maine, announced on Facebook that its last day open would be February 2.
The Facebook post stated the restaurant had been open for nearly 12 years and thanked the staff and customers for a "memorable ride." Henry's Public House via Facebook Henry's Public House Henry's Public House in Portland, Maine, announced on Facebook it would be closing on February 15.
The post also thanked its employees: "We are forever indebted to all the staff who worked so hard to make Henry's what it is." Google Maps HiFi Donuts HiFi Donuts in Portland, Maine, announced in March on Facebook that it would be leaving its downtown location in April. Its last day was April 17.
The reason for the closure? Turns out, they were unable to negotiate a lease agreement.
That said, this isn't the end of HIFi Donuts as they are now looking for a new location to set up shop.
The downtown Portland spot opened in 2017. Hotel Rumford via Facebook Hotel Rumford The Hotel Rumford in Rumford, Maine, announced on Facebook that it would close on February 15.
The landmark spot has been around since 1888.
Big twist: the place reopened under new management in September 2025 . Lee Frank's Wells Lee Frank's According to the Portland Press Herald , Lee Frank's closed its location in Wells in September.
The restaurant opened in October 2024.
There are two other Lee Frank's locations in South Berwick, Maine, and Exeter, New Hampshire. leda.portland via Instagram Leda According to an Instagram post , Leda in Portland, Maine, said it would be closing on October 27, 2025.
The owner of the cafe shared that "unfortunately, the business has reached a point where it’s no longer financially sustainable in our current location."
Leda opened in May 2025. littlebrotherchinesefood via Facebook Little Brother Chinese Food Little Brother Chinese Food in South Portland, Maine, announced on January 10 on Instagram that it would be closing after four years of operations.
Read more here. lorenasempanadas via Instagram Lorena’s Empanadas According to an Instagram post , Lorena's Empanadas in York, Maine, would be closing on October 26, 2025.
The restaurant's owner shared that "it was a very difficult decision for me to make but due to personal life changes, it’s what I have to do." She did add that she hopes to reopen at some point in the future.
Lorena's Empanadas opened in 2023. Low Stakes Lodge via Facebook Low Stakes Lodge According to a Facebook post , Low Stakes Lodge in Portland, Maine, closed on October 20, 2025.
The steakhouse said in an Instagram post that it was going to be turned into The Highroller Lobster Co.
Low Stakes Lodge opened in 2024. Luiggi's Pizzeria via Facebook Luiggi's Pizzeria According to a Facebook post on August 25 , Luiggi's Pizzeria in Lewiston confirmed that the sad rumors were true and the pizza place would be closing permanently.
The eatery said in the post that they were "truly sorry we couldn’t keep the nostalgia going the way many had hoped."
They acknowledged the many hurdles they faced after taking over the 72-year-old restaurant from its previous owners, but they wanted to focus on the positive and the memories, grateful for being a part of the decades-long legacy. Macks Restaurant and Tavern via Facebook Mack's Restaurant and Tavern According to a Facebook post , Mack's Restaurant and Tavern in Brewer, Maine, announced it would be closing on November 23, 2025.
The restaurant said it faced several challenges, including "the lack of consistent community support, the hard times so many are facing right now, and the constant negative comments and misinformation spread about us," as well as being unable to obtain an amusement license.
Mack's Restaurant and Tavern opened in April 2025. Maine Craft Distilling via Facebook Maine Craft Distilling Maine Craft Distilling announced on Facebook in January that it was closing The Public House in Portland for the winter, but that became permanent.
According to Portland Food Map in March, the restaurant and tasting room would stay closed, and Maine Craft Distilling would instead focus on their canned cocktail business, which now makes up about 90 percent of their sales. Mast Landing Brewing Company (South Portland) via Facebook Mast Landing Brewing Company According to an Instagram post , Mast Landing Brewing Company announced it would be closing its South Portland taproom on December 31, 2025.
This particular location opened in 2023.
In the Instagram post, they noted it was not an easy decision, but it will let them "dedicate our focus and resources to strengthening our Freeport and Westbrook locations."
Mast Landing Brewing Company started in 2015. My Buddy's Place via Facebook My Buddy's Place My Buddy's Place shared on Facebook that it would be closing on September 30, 2025, "due to a variety of ongoing issues, one of them being health."
The restaurant opened in Bucksport, Maine, in 2024. Google Maps Oak & Ember Oak & Ember in Buxton, Maine, announced on Instagram on April 11 that "with the heaviest of hearts we announce our closure."
While the exact reasoning for the eatery's ending wasn't revealed, thanks and appreciation were shared in the Instagram post for the people who showed up and supported them.
The farm-to-table restaurant opened in 2023. Obscura Café & Drinkery via Facebook; Canva Obscura Café & Drinkery Obscura Café & Drinkery in Lewiston, Maine, announced on Facebook in May that it would be closed at the end of June.
The spot mentioned that "the ongoing challenges we faced with the city, and the current declining conditions and safety of the area have just proven insurmountable for us."
Read more here. Paper Tiger via Facebook Paper Tiger According to an Instagram post , Paper Tiger in Portland announced that its last day would be August 31.
The cocktail bar and restaurant, which served creative cocktails and small plate dishes, opened in 2022.
In its post, Paper Tiger shared the news "with a heavy heart and a real sense of accomplishment," but acknowledged their love for the people who came to enjoy the little Portland spot. Pop’s Place via Facebook Pop’s Place Pop's Place in Windham, Maine, shared on the Windham Maine Community Facebook group a post that after two years it would be closing on February 8.
The post cited "lack of quality and qualified workers, increasing prices and decreasing demands" as part of the decision. Pilots Cove Cafe via Facebook Pilots Cove Cafe According to a Facebook post , Pilots Cove Cafe in Sanford, Maine, announced it would be closing on November 23, 2025.
The cafe thanked everyone for their time at the spot but noted that they are opening a new place in Alfred in 2026.
Pilots Cove Cafe opened in 2019. Rebel Munchies & Libations via Facebook Rebel Munchies & Libations Rebel Munchies & Libations in Portland, Maine, closed unexpectedly in January, according to Portland Old Port .
It also noted that the restaurant had only been open for less than a year before the closure.
Read more here. Google Maps Richie Ribeye's While Richie Ribeye's in Westbrook, Maine, didn't have a closing announcement, it did post on Facebook on January 18 that the business was for sale.
Read more here. Rosemont Market and Bakery via Facebook Rosemont Market and Bakery Rosemont Market and Bakery in Portland, Maine, announced on January 15 on its Facebook page that the Congress Street location would be closing after 17 years.
It noted that "operational challenges in the store’s smaller space have grown over time," but there are still six other locations to visit, including two in Portland.
Read more here. Google Maps Ruby Tuesday The Bangor Daily News reported on November 4, 2025, that Ruby Tuesday in Presque Isle, Maine, had closed.
At that time, only a Brewer and Waterville Ruby Tuesday remained. Jeff Tuttle, Townsquare Media Ruby Tuesday According to i95rocks.com , Ruby Tuesday in Brewer, Maine, closed in November 2025, not long after the Presque Isle location.
What started as a temporary closure became permanent, leaving Waterville with the last Ruby Tuesday in the state. Sagamore Hill Lounge via Facebook Sagamore Hill Lounge According to a Facebook post , Sagamore Hill Lounge in Portland, Maine, announced it would be closing on December 31, 2025.
It first opened in 2018.
In the social media post, the Teddy Roosevelt-inspired bar noted "life is taking us in a new direction and we’re moving on." Secundo via Facebook Secundo Secundo in South Berwick, Maine, announced on Facebook that it would be closing June 2.
The Italian restaurant thanked its patrons and staff members for making it a special place. Serendib via Facebook Serendib According to a Facebook post , Serendib in Ellsworth, Maine, announced it would be closing on December 20, 2025.
It first opened in 2015.
In the post , the restaurant's owners noted that while it is time for new adventures, "Introducing Sri Lankan cuisine to the Downeast region of Maine has been a pure joy and the reception from the community has been incredible." sisslewinebar via Instagram Sissle & Daughters Sissle & Daughters on Forest Avene in Portland, Maine, announced on Instagram it would be closing on February 22.
The post revealed the closing was due to sudden and personal reasons but the Sissle & Daughters Cheesemongers on Washington Avenue would still be open. Stars & Stripes Brewing Company via Facebook Stars & Stripes Brewing Company Stars & Stripes Brewing Company in Freeport, Maine's last day was technically December 31, 2024, but we wanted to include it on this list since it was the last day of the year leading into 2025.
The brewery made the announcement on its Facebook page in September 2024.
Read more here. Susan's Fish & Chips via Facebook Susan's Fish & Chips According to a Facebook post , Susan's Fish & Chips in Portland, Maine, announced it would be closing on October 30, 2025.
The restaurant said it was sad to close but, "times have changed the cost of products, the increase in wages and the overall costs make it very difficult."
Susan's opened in 1989. trinkenbrewingco via Instagram Trinken Brewing Co. According to an Instagram post , Trinken Brewing Co. in West Bath, Maine, said it would close on October 31, 2025.
They thanked their staff and customers for "nearly 6 incredible years."
Trinken Brewing Co. opened in 2020. The Yahweh Cafe & Bakery LLC via Facebook The Yahweh Cafe & Bakery According to the Bangor Daily News , Yahweh Cafe & Bakery in Bangor, Maine, closed on November 18, 2025.
The newspaper said that it was closing due to a lack of customers and overhead costs.
Yahweh Cafe & Bakery in September 2025. Wessie’s Den via Facebook Wessie’s Den According to a Facebook post , Wessie's Den in Westbrook, Maine, shared that it would be closing on October 31, 2025.
The arcade bar thanked its customers and noted that it would love to pass on the torch if anyone was interested in carrying things on.
Wessie's Den opened in 2022. wileysgoodfood via Instagram Wiley's Good Food In an Instagram post , Wiley's announced it would be closing September 6, 2025.
The breakfast and lunch stand in Rockland, Maine, opened in 2023.
The owner of Wiley's said in the Instagram post that he is "blessed and thankful for this community and the tremendous growth I’ve experienced as a person and as a business."
He also added that this is simply the closing of one chapter and not a goodbye but rather a "see you later." Whittle Bird Coffee via Facebook Whittle Bird According to a Facebook post , Whittle Bird in Dover-Foxcroft closed on August 30, 2025.
The coffee and baked goods spot opened in 2024. Zaozemaine via Facebook Zao ze According to a Facebook post , ZaoZe Cafe and Market in Brunswick, Maine, announced it would close on November 1, 2025.
The cafe said that "the hospitality landscape has changed in many ways, and after careful consideration, we believe this is the right time to close this chapter."
ZaoZe Cafe opened in 2020.
